Indian Railways has been spotted running trains with containers stacked three high, as shown in a widely shared video of a freight movement under electrified tracks. The footage, circulating as evidence of “triple stack container trains,” depicts specialized shorter and wider boxes rather than standard ISO shipping containers. 

These dwarf-style units are designed for high-volume, lighter cargo such as plastics and FMCG goods, allowing three layers while remaining within existing overhead wire clearances.

Such configurations have been tested and used on select routes for several years, including documented trials of dwarf and cuboid containers around 2021. They differ from the recent official milestone of long-haul double-stack operations on the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, which use regular containers on purpose-built high-rise infrastructure. The video confirms an existing capability with non-standard containers, not a new nationwide rollout of triple-stacking conventional boxes.
